Major markets like Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Kolkata demonstrated positive trends, while NCR faced a significant decline. Higher-ticket homes are increasingly preferred, with sales of properties priced above Rs 1 crore climbing sharply. Sales for lower-priced segments, however, experienced a downturn, reducing buyers' options.

A firmer dollar was observed, approaching a 17-month high due to a weak euro's impact. Crude oil prices increased to nearly $103 per barrel, posing risks to India's economy. Early data shows a notable increase in taxable supplies after these reforms, positively impacting both businesses and consumers, with small and medium enterprises particularly benefiting from a cohesive national market.

items.title: RBI could keep rates higher for longer amid global and local risks
items.summary: With global financial risks in the spotlight, the Reserve Bank of India is indicating a shift towards higher interest rates. Governor Sanjay Malhotra has highlighted emerging challenges, including significant global debt levels and surging asset prices. The rise in US treasury yields and crude oil costs suggests trials ahead for the Indian economy.

items.title: The oil shock hasn’t stopped the factory boom. It may be changing what factories make | Explained
items.summary: Oil and other energy costs are still feeding into transport, electricity and industrial inputs. Factory selling prices are rising at one of their fastest rates in more than three years. So why are manufacturers still expanding?

items.title: India's strong growth fundamentals face risks from prolonged external shocks: Erik Berglof
items.summary: India's growth prospects remain strong despite external shocks affecting the economy. Erik Berglof highlights the need for resilience against climate and geopolitical risks. He notes that high US bond yields could impact emerging economies due to higher interest costs. Additionally, energy and water security are identified as critical areas needing improvement.

items.title: Capital limited but confidence in rules of trade, fiscal path of large economies: DEA secretary
items.summary: Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur said trade shaped by security and geopolitical considerations could deepen global imbalances, raise capital costs and create friction. She said private investment was showing signs of revival despite tight global financial conditions, while the AI investment cycle was adding to demand for capital and debt.

items.title: Cinepolis adds four more screens in Faridabad as its big-screen expansion continues across Delhi-NCR
items.summary: Cinepolis India has opened a four-screen multiplex at Amolik’s City Life Mall in Faridabad, taking its presence in the city to eight screens as it expands across Delhi-NCR with a focus on growing urban catchments.

items.title: India within striking distance of 8% GDP growth, resilience not accidental: Shaktikanta Das
items.summary: With an ambitious target of 8% GDP growth, India aims for Viksit Bharat by the year 2047 through innovative reforms. The government is dedicated to increasing domestic capabilities in crucial areas such as energy and manufacturing. Significant measures are being implemented to strengthen long-term finance and bolster involvement in global supply chains.

items.title: Airbus flags A330 jets for stray tools: Why airlines are being asked to inspect aircraft
items.summary: Airbus SE has requested airlines to conduct extra checks on A330neo aircraft. This reportedly affects A330s built from 2021 to July 2026, complicating the identification of impacted aircraft.

items.title: GST exemption for banks, nominated agencies for gold, silver imports may be withdrawn
items.summary: The GST Council may end the IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imported by banks and nominated agencies, sources said. The exemption, introduced in 2017 when precious-metal imports were tightly regulated, could be withdrawn as the government seeks to curb non-essential imports and manage foreign exchange outflows.

items.title: Haldia Petrochemicals-arm Adperma plans public listing, downstream expansion, says MD Navanit Narayan
items.summary: Haldia Petrochemicals subsidiary Adperma is considering an initial public offering to fund its expansion into specialty chemicals and advanced polymers.

items.title: GST Council may clear sweeping compliance reforms; e-commerce sellers, genuine buyers to get relief
items.summary: The GST Council will assess various procedural reforms aimed at simplifying tax compliance for businesses. Proposed measures include enabling small e-commerce vendors to register using platform warehouses. Additionally, the input tax credit for genuine buyers will be protected even if suppliers fail to remit tax.

items.title: Employers may soon be able to claim ITC on GST paid for employee insurance cover
items.summary: The GST Council is gearing up to consider a proposal regarding input tax credit for employee insurance premiums. Currently, businesses cannot claim input tax credit on insurance policies purchased for their employees. An 18 percent GST is imposed on these group insurance policies, impacting business expenses.

items.title: RBI likely to raise repo rate in October 2026 as West Asia crisis fuels inflation risks
items.summary: Experts poll: RBI may increase rates by 0.25 pc in Oct policy amid inflationary pressures

items.title: IndiaTech seeks rethink of turnover-linked gig worker social security levy
items.summary: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, aggregators are required to contribute 1-2% of annual turnover towards social security for gig and platform workers, subject to a cap of 5% of the amount paid or payable to such workers.

items.title: GST 2.0's next move: Council may scrap officers' arrest powers, raise prosecution bar to Rs 5 crore
items.summary: The GST Council is weighing changes to GST enforcement, including ending officials' arrest powers and shifting to court-ordered arrests. Criminal prosecution may be limited to cases involving more than Rs 5 crore, while routine disputes over GST interpretation could be handled through civil penalties and kept outside criminal courts.

items.title: Sports betting is increasingly the norm for Gen Z. Here’s why some financial and mental health experts are worried
items.summary: Surveys show Gen Z increasingly views sports bets as a form of investment, and those who gamble too often face mental health risks.

items.title: Trump taps Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as AI czar
items.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will lead the administration's AI policy.

items.title: GST arrest powers may be removed? Council to discuss decriminalisation on Wednesday; law change likely in Winter Session
items.summary: GST enforcement could see a major shift as the Centre and states weigh changes to arrest powers under the indirect tax regime. The proposal comes amid concerns over how these provisions have been used against businesses. Here’s what could change and what it means.

items.title: Easy money era is ending, interest rates to stay high: French economist Landau
items.summary: French economist Jean-Pierre Landau says falling savings, rising investment needs and heavy public debt could keep real interest rates structurally higher.

items.title: DLF sells out maiden senior living project Aureva in Gurugram for ₹1,985 cr
items.summary: Average ticket size of an apartment at The Aureva is ₹11.5 crore, at ₹28,000 per sq ft. Each residence is complemented by three parking spaces and access to a suite of wellness, recreational, and lifestyle amenities.

items.title: Investors look to shelter portfolios from rising AI concentration risks
items.summary: Fund managers see hedge funds and emerging markets assets as bulwarks against sudden shift in sentiment on artificial intelligence

items.title: India’s growth is making the world rewrite its forecast: MoSPI Secretary Saurabh Garg
items.summary: India's continued economic resilience, supported by strong corporate performance and sustained investment activity, is now being reflected in upward revisions to the country's growth estimates by various international agencies, Saurabh Garg, Secretary, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), said.

items.title: Angel One is shrinking. But what is it building?
items.summary: For over 30 years, Angel One has adapted to a changing brokerage landscape. Now, regulatory pressure and intensifying competition are forcing another reset. Where does Angel One go from here?

items.summary: Market Questions is the FT’s guide to the week ahead

items.title: Lockheed Martin’s India expansion plan hinges on $10.5bn military aircraft bid: Which firms are competing for project?
items.summary: Lockheed Martin plans to expand its manufacturing in India if it wins a $10.5 billion contract for 60 medium transport aircraft. It has partnered with Tata Advanced Systems and aims to deliver 12 aircraft initially, while 48 will be produced locally, enhancing India's aviation capabilities.

items.title: Why the IPO market is booming and busting
items.summary: Flotations have stalled and returns from new listings have been weak

items.title: RBI may increase rates by 0.25 pc in Oct policy amid inflationary pressures, experts poll shows
items.summary: The RBI is expected to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points in its October policy review as inflation pressures build from higher crude prices, the West Asia conflict and global monetary tightening, according to a PTI poll of economists and bankers. Most also expect a hawkish tone, a higher FY27 inflation forecast and possibly further rate hikes later in the fiscal year.

items.title: GVC integration, supply chain resilience, FTAs key to boost exports, high-end manufacturing: Deloitte India
items.summary: India needs deeper integration into global value chains, lower logistics costs and better use of free trade agreements to boost exports and move into higher-value manufacturing, according to Deloitte India. It also called for stronger supply-chain resilience, tariff rationalisation and greater support for MSMEs facing trade-finance, compliance and currency risks.

items.title: US to receive potash shipment from Belarus as relations thaw
items.summary: Washington has begun to ease sanctions on Minsk in exchange for the release of political prisoners

items.title: India’s food market: $600 bn estimate; 7% CAGR — from primary producer to high-value global processing powerhouse
items.summary: Experts said India was moving from a primary producer to a high-value global processing powerhouse to double agri-food exports beyond the current US$53 billion benchmark through value addition and market access unlocked by the India–EU Free Trade Agreement.

items.title: South Korean president orders probe into data leaks across financial industry
items.summary: SOUTHKOREA-HACK:South Korean president orders probe into data leaks across financial industry

items.title: Singapore debuts a state-backed dating app for young government workers as it works to slow a demographic crisis
items.summary: Singapore's government is playing matchmaker for young public officials against a backdrop of ultra-low fertility.

items.title: Ukraine’s surprise robot offensive exposes a vulnerability in Putin’s war machine
items.summary: Experts say the offensive is not a decisive breakthrough, but demonstrates how Ukraine’s expanding use of robotic systems is reshaping frontline warfare.

items.title: Wall Street’s IPO fervour cools on tepid demand and valuation worries
items.summary: Several listings have been paused in recent weeks as delay in Anthropic’s public debut sends a chill through markets

items.title: Industrial marketplace Pneucons disables UPI on orders from Oct 10, co-founder says ‘MDR ate 94% of our margins’
items.summary: Starting October 10, Pneucons will discontinue UPI payments after government imposed a 0.4% MDR charge on orders over ₹2,000, which the company's co-founder says will take a significant toll on its margins. Details here.

items.title: Adani Airport to go ahead with Mumbai redevelopment; airlines reject proposal
items.summary: Adani Airports chief executive Arun Bansal has assured airlines that the shift to Navi Mumbai airport is temporary. The airlines said their support for Terminal 1 redevelopment could not be construed as consent to the proposed reduction in international slots

items.title: Fleur to deploy $1 bn as Lemon Tree splits ownership, management businesses
items.summary: The planned separation will allow Lemon Tree to focus on asset-light hotel management, franchising and branding, while Fleur takes on the capital-intensive business of owning and developing hotels.

items.title: Intesa Says Paschi Bid to Lapse If Holders Back Rival Deals
items.summary: Intesa Sanpaolo SpA said its offer for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA will lapse if Paschi shareholders back either of its proposed bids for Banco BPM SpA and Banca Generali SpA at an Oct. 29 meeting.

items.title: Meta’s AI Data Center tax strategy that saves billions - Report
items.summary: The debate over Meta's strategy therefore comes down to whether its massive AI infrastructure projects represent genuine experimentation for tax purposes or simply the construction and operation of expensive data centres.

items.title: Not lack of talent, senior business leaders point to these key factors posing obstacles...
items.summary: Only 5% of leaders attribute execution gaps to talent shortages, a survey by Biz Staffing Comrade revealed. The primary obstacles holding organisations back they felt are shifting priorities and outdated processes.

items.title: ‘No place to grow artificial minds’: Why did David Robinson quit OpenAI? What did he write in his essay?
items.summary: David Robinson published a scathing essay in The Atlantic, accusing OpenAI’s ‘unimpeded optimism’ of fostering a hazardous environment for advanced technology

items.title: FM Sitharaman calls for open, predictable global economic ties amid rising uncertainty
items.summary: Finance minister Sitharaman said geopolitical tensions, trade barriers and thinner buffers are reshaping the global economy, while urging greater private investment in India.

items.title: Lula or Bolsonaro: Wall Street braces for two wildly different results in Brazil election
items.summary: With the first round of Brazil's presidential election taking place Sunday, Wall Street is gearing up with starkly different market predictions.

items.title: America’s data center fight is a preview of what's to come for the rest of the world
items.summary: America’s fight over data centers is going global. Communities across Europe and Asia are pushing back over the rising costs of the AI infrastructure boom.

items.title: FlyDubai plane attack by co-pilot was an attempted 'terrorist' act, UAE says
items.summary: The FlyDubai co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the UAE prosecutor general said.

items.title: Private capital is reshaping Hollywood moviemaking
items.summary: As Hollywood's financing structures diversify, private capital is increasingly funding the big screen and changing the types of movies that are being made.
